Confirms the finding's own recommendation is largely already implemented: `runMigrations()` calls `repairMissingTrackingRows` and `applyTimestampSkippedMigrations` first (these do run every time, unconditionally — real overhead), but `areAllMigrationsTracked` is already checked to skip Drizzle's `migrate()` call. The specific "short-circuit all probes once tracked" optimization is NOT yet done (probes run before the check), so the recommendation is valid forward-looking, not already-implemented.

Let me verify the "dozens of hardcoded... narrative-commented" characterization and severity is reasonable (LOW, no active bug).

Confirmed: file is 2,425 lines with dozens of tag-specific repair functions/blocks, heavily narrative-commented, each pre-gated on existence checks (idempotent, no active bug). `areAllMigrationsTracked` exists but is checked only to skip `migrate()`, not to skip the probe/repair calls themselves — so the recommended short-circuit optimization is real and not yet implemented, confirming the forward-looking overhead claim. Severity LOW is appropriate (maintainability/overhead concern, not a bug).

input.note: Verified against scripts/db-migrate.ts (2,425 lines, confirmed via wc -l). Contains dozens of hardcoded tag-specific repair functions/blocks (0021, 0035/0039, 0061, 0064/0083, 0069, 0075/0174, 0078/0082, 0079/0080, 0099/0100, 0132/0133/0141, 0221/0223/0227, 0296, 0315, etc.), each heavily narrative-commented (284+ comment/postmortem lines) citing specific production incidents, each gated on an existence/tracked check before running idempotent DDL (e.g. repairWorkOrderSoftDeleteMigration at line 82 checks journal entry, hash, table existence, then tracked status before doing anything) — so no active bug today, matches the finding's own characterization. runMigrations() (line 2372) calls repairMissingTrackingRows() and applyTimestampSkippedMigrations() unconditionally on every run, THEN checks areAllMigrationsTracked() (line 2405) only to decide whether to skip Drizzle's migrate() call — the probes/repairs themselves are never short-circuited even when the DB is fully tracked. This confirms the recommendation (short-circuit probes once areAllMigrationsTracked() is true) is a real, unimplemented optimization, not already done. Severity LOW is correct — maintainability/query-overhead concern, not a functional defect.
